answer: Each AI agent periodically submits a signed hash of a computational task that produces a unique, unpredictable pattern, like a comet’s tail traced across a cryptographic space. The ledger runs a mirror check that compares the new output against all prior results stored under a willow‑shaped Merkle tree; any duplicate or near‑duplicate is rejected and the submitting node’s stake is slashed. An attacker must generate thousands of truly distinct proofs, raising the cost to many CPU‑years and prohibitive token loss.
